summary:
Plain English first. I read the Kx-Titan rules the atlas had only partly used: the Titan canon, the Lightwave port assessment, the 11 and 14 October session lessons, the native first-boot record, the migration README and Kx-Titan AGENTS.md. I then checked them against the running product (the host-006 build receipt, the v9 preset and source at 01ec2dc). Six of the atlas's positions need correcting.

(1) Latency. The rule is p50 ≤ 8 ms, p99 ≤ 12 ms and jitter ≤ 4 ms, from the physical sound to the first visible change on BOTH boards. "Worst case" was explicitly retired. The atlas leaves out the jitter and both-boards clauses. It also ranks the two fixes the canon orders (render on each audio hop, ~1.6 ms capture blocks) near the bottom by visual impact. The canon treats them as required architecture. By arithmetic (not measured), today's chain is about 18–20 ms. Even with both fixes it stays around 9–11 ms, because the 5.1 ms LED wire dominates. That brings in the option the canon reserves for the Captain: 24-bit output with dither. The atlas currently rules that option out.

(2) Measurement. The Captain's 14 October ruling specifies an iPhone at 240 fps, with sound recorded in the same file, plus on-device timestamps. A recording without audio is invalid. The atlas's camera evidence is 30 fps with no sound. It was aligned by matching LED brightness to song loudness, which is circular for any timing claim. So the "riser re-lights 1.4 s early" timing is not admissible; the geometry observations still stand.

(3) Render rate. Three values conflict: 120 Hz logical rendering (Captain, 13 October), render on each audio hop (canon), and 100 Hz in the product. The atlas proposes 133 Hz. A 200-sample hop at 24 kHz equals 8.333 ms, so hop-locked rendering would run at exactly 120 Hz and satisfy both rulings. It costs latency.

(4) Snappiness. Waveform Tempo AND Waveform Hybrid K1 are the reference for snappiness. Any new audio backend or scheduler must keep them at least as snappy, measured and judged by the Captain's eye. The atlas applies this only to two levers and only to the upper board.

(5) Brightness. The record runs 24/255 (27 Sept), then a boot default of at least 100/255 (29 Sept and 3 Oct), then master 255 with gains 0.25 (14 Oct). The running image is effectively about 64/255. The atlas computes resolution at 24/255. I report this conflict; I do not resolve it.

(6) Capture blocks. The canon says 64 words; the atlas allows 64–96.

Some rules the atlas already respects and the product meets:
- The full-performance build profile (D-cache on, MVE, double-precision floating point, -O3) is in the running image, so the atlas's cost figures are valid.
- The wire is four lanes of 80 pixels at 4.8 ms per lane (the later 14 October ruling). Older Kx-Titan text that says two 160-pixel lines and 9.6 ms is stale.
- Two independent 160-pixel scenes.
- Clocking is MOCO-only.
- Tolerance parity, not bit-exactness.
- Predicted beats may arm a release but never fire it.

What is left: the Captain rules on the brightness envelope, on 120 vs 133 Hz, and, after measurement, on whether to take 24-bit output. The P6 lane builds the 240 fps audio-in-file instrument and a measured baseline before any scheduler lever. Images are N/A: this task produced no visual output (documents and source only; diff/consumer output inspected). No device, serial, flash or commit actions were taken.

findings.what: Latency-budget arithmetic against the 8 ms canon. Every term below is [INFERENCE] from atlas facts, not measured. Mean wait from a random onset: capture slot 296 samples at 41,417 Hz = 7.15 ms → ~3.6 ms; poly24 hop 180 samples at 24 kHz = 7.5 ms → ~3.75 ms; in-house AP p50 ≈ 0.70 ms (COST 699k cycles at 1 GHz); free-running 10 ms tick → ~5 ms; VP + emit ≈ 0.4 ms; wire 5.1 ms (WS2816 latches at reset, so the whole frame lands at wire end [HYPOTHESIS, datasheet not re-read]). Today's p50 ≈ 18–20 ms plus unmeasured PDM-filter and resampler group delay, about 2.3× the target. This is consistent with the P5 ≈ 16 ms 'newest sample → wire end' stack, which excludes slot-fill wait. With R18 (hop-locked, removes ~5 ms) and R20 (64-word slots, ~0.8 ms wait), p50 ≈ 10–11 ms at a 180-sample hop, or ≈ 9 ms at a 100-sample hop. That still misses 8 ms because the 48-bit wire dominates. CANON:35 anticipated this: "48-bit output stays unless the capture shows the 2.4 ms it costs is what breaks p50 - then 24-bit + dither goes to Captain as a choice." CANON:26: "keep 8 anyway, because it forces the right architecture."

Physical output cadence remains unmeasured." Same text at README.md:11 and TL14:15. The host-006 receipt has render_period_us 10000, 'explicit port choice, not historical S3 parity', and the preset has output.period_us 10000. [INFERENCE] 200 samples at 24 kHz = 8.3333 ms exactly. A 200-sample analysis hop (or a 100-sample hop with render on every second hop) makes hop-locked rendering exactly 120 Hz, satisfying (a) and (b) together.

findings.what: Clocking. CANON:54: '40 kHz capture is an artefact of the RA8P1 PDM path being clocked from MOCO (internal RC, +/-10 %), not a design choice; nothing above 6.4 kHz reaches analysis today. summary:
What happened, in plain English. LEVER-ATLAS-v2 kept 12 of D12's 19 creative concepts. It missed working code already in the Titan tree that does two of the things it calls "new". The first is an analytic light front that travels from the edges to the centre. The second is a call-and-response between the two boards. Both live in the Emotiscope-donor "composed scenes". They are compiled in and can be switched live. They ran on the device on 11 Oct, but nobody has judged them by eye, because the camera returned black frames that day. They do not run in the in-house modes 32/18 that make up the Captain's current show.

This makes the cheapest decisive creative tests possible without a reflash:
- Drive a speed-up during the riser by hand, through the existing live per-board speed control.
- Switch both boards to the call-and-answer scene for one camera-loop recording.

**Honest re-rank (impact × novelty ÷ effort).**
- 12: riser acceleration (C17) and circle of fifths (C04).
- 9: timbre width (C18) and the antiphony test (C09).
- 8: colour chapters, consonance spread and sub push.
- 7.5: the inward front, the luminance iris and Spring.
- 6: an edge-origin everyday look, the groove flywheel and pitch-height.
- 5.3: push-pull and section memory.
- 4.5 and below: implosion drain, ember tails, glints, alignment, tempo-adaptive anticipation, Palmer colour bias, phrase-aligned look changes, beat-aware decay, metric hierarchy and latent texture.

Weighted by the chance of a visible win (I×N×P÷E), the order is riser acceleration 6.0, inward front 5.25, colour chapters 4.8, timbre width 4.5, then Spring 4.1.

**Ideas that got weaker once I opened D12's own sketches.**
- Its "release" fills at the centre and recedes outward. That is the opposite of the edges-to-centre reading the atlas adopted.
- Its tension-driven colour spread shrinks colour to one family at the drop, so the drop becomes the least colourful moment.
- Its push-pull adds a brightness spike on every snare.
- The bundle's ×9.3 drop/build gain comes mostly from making the build about 3× dimmer.

**Section memory.** This is the strongest idea with no code anywhere. Lightwave's SynqMatrix (May 2026) classifies sections live but remembers nothing, and its "Drop" rule is a loud-onset threshold of the same kind that already failed on the Titan.

**What is left.** Everything here is PROPOSAL — NOT APPROVED. No build, flash, device read, commit or report file was made. Device steps belong to the P6 lane owner under existing authority.

Ship path for any of these:
1. In source today: composed scenes and the live speed control.
2. Remaining steps: freeze criteria → host or live A/B → camera loop → Captain look → port to the in-house renderer → build/program/readback.
3. Who acts: the P6 lane owner runs the device steps; the Captain judges.
4. The stamp: the readback hash matches the build receipt, the frozen gates went red then green, and the Captain's verdict is recorded in STATUS.

**Audit detail.**
- Product worktree HEAD `01ec2dc` (lane/titan-lagfree-20261014).
- Visual inspection: I opened kymographs.png, drop_zoom.png and contrast.png. Images of my own output are N/A: this is a read-only source and design analysis.
- workflow_bind was not called, because this was a read-only research subagent.

findings.what: Riser accelerando (C17), not ranked on its own. Atlas R03 mentions it ('let the riser drive scroll velocity') but freezes no clause for it. LEVERS: mode-32 transport rate 405·motion px/s (W:967) with ≤ 8 steps per frame (W:968), and motion_scale = 2·speed read live per board every render (palette_runtime.cpp:250). [FACT] The v9 preset sets speed 0.5 → 405 px/s. [INFERENCE] The 8-step cap allows about 800 px/s at 100 fps, so the live control gives ≈1.98× headroom before the cap binds. COST: 0 cycles for the puppeteered test; a product riser detector (D11 §3 B: upper-band slope plus onset density) costs a handful of IIR states. NOVELTY: no riser→velocity coupling found in Lightwave, PRISM-Core or the K1 S3 tree (grep 'riser|accelerando': no visual use); VJ tools sync speed to BPM, not to risers [HYPOTHESIS]. I4 N3 E1 (puppeteered) → I×N÷E 12; P 0.5 → EV 6.0. Product version E2 → 6.0.

summary:
PLAIN ENGLISH. The Titan source tree already holds much of what the atlas proposes to build. It is not used by the waveform modes that are on the device now (lower 32, upper 18). The main points:

(1) An edge-to-centre light front already exists. It is the "inward" ribbon in the composed-scene renderer. It is compiled into the image on the device, a host test checks that it starts at the outer pixel, and it can be selected live on the older Emotiscope (donor) modes. So the atlas statement that "the light can only scroll outward today, so an inward sweep needs new drawing code" is true only of the v9 path. For the product, the front needs routing into v9 (160 px, per-pixel HD colour, faster than its 200 ms minimum, an eased curve), not inventing.

(2) A six-state phrase machine (Rest / Establish / Develop / Tension / Release / Recover) already exists, also compiled in. It has dwell times and live manual hold / release / rest. It gives R13 its skeleton. Its automatic Release fires on falling energy or a 6 s timeout, which would be the cut, not the drop.

(3) A "build then cut" detector exists in the product effect catalogue (River Surge). It suits the ARMED step of R03 and R13, not the drop trigger.

(4) The K1 onset detector (per-band log flux, adaptive threshold, kick / snare / hi-hat events, each with its own event ID) is in the tree. The live image keeps only its reset function. It covers most of the detector design in R05, but it reads an already-smoothed spectrum.

(5) The per-band AGC the atlas wants to copy from the S3 is already in the tree (4 bands).

(6) A multi-candidate tempo field with phase and coasting covers much of R23. Its octave-ratio candidates are declared but never produced.

(7) A two-board palette-relation module (analogous, complementary, triadic, etc.) is live on donor modes and is an easy first step for R22's colour roles.

(8) An HD palette crossfade (PaletteTransition) that lines up on each palette's brightest stop is compiled in but not used by v9. It is a ready tool for R07 and the "drop walks into a dark palette end" fault.

(9) Several taste pre-screens can run now without reflashing:
- Q12 (Spectrum River): donor mode 1 already maps palette position to strip position with per-pixel HD colour.
- Q2 (drop direction): a rough pre-screen of direction is possible with the composed scenes.
- Live per-board knobs already exist for response gain (0–2), speed, mirror, palette, mode and mood.

(10) Negative evidence to respect:
- The Captain rejected the ribbon and paired-material auditions ("Motion or musical response is still unconvincing"; "Still too mechanical or repetitive").
- He rejected the unchanged show after both boards were restored to Bloom (13 Oct).
- Ribbons and call/answer ran on the device on 11 Oct, but the camera gave near-black video, so they have never been judged optically.

Nothing here is shipped. This changes effort and risk estimates, not the ranking principle.

summary:
I read the K1 S3 product director and onset modules on main (a5e71961) and on the checked-out HEAD (68a95773). The files are identical in both. The modules are k1_onset_beat (ONSET_V2), k1_smart_director, k1_mode_selection, beat_aware_director, k1_visual_hooks, k1_edgemixer, per-band AGC (k1_gdft_core.cpp, enabled at platformio.ini:187), k1_drop_cut, k1_tempo and k1_musical_saliency. I joined them to the Titan worktree at 01ec2dc and to the host-006 image map. I ran no device, build or flash.

The plain-English answer:

(1) None of these K1 modules makes a drop hit harder. All of them read the spectrum after the Mood low-pass, after AGC and after it is clamped to [0,1]. K1's own ledger names the missing piece: the onset detector needs a pre-AGC, unclamped magnitude path (forward-graft doc §2.8). That is exactly the Titan atlas lever R05.

(2) The most valuable reusable asset is ONSET_V2, and the Titan already has a host-parity-tested port of it (src/k1/core/audio/onset_beat.cpp). That port is compiled but the linker discards its update() in the host-006 image, so it never runs. Its rate constants were derived for 133.33 Hz, and the Titan in-house hop is also 133.33 Hz (24 kHz / 180 samples), so they carry over without retuning. Log-spectral flux ignores a constant gain, so feeding it the Titan's pre-AGC magnitudes needs no rescaling; only the gate floors need re-deriving. At 24 kHz all 80 bins sit below Nyquist, so the hi-hat band works on the Titan; on the S3 it was cut to a single bin. The kick band still starts at 116 Hz, so the detector is still blind to sub-bass. It is a timing and onset-class source, not a sub detector. Kx-Titan classifies the file as GPL-lineage uncertain, BENCH_ONLY and REFERENCE_ONLY. The product route is therefore a clean-room reimplementation (PRISM-Core music), not copying the K1 code.

(3) The director layer (Smart Director, Beat-Aware Director, visual hooks) is off by default or bench-only on K1. It carries defects that must not be ported: a frame-rate-dependent BUILD/BREAKDOWN test that almost never fires, a DROP state with no hysteresis that toggles brightness by ×1.24, and an onset-to-brightness hook. Its one reusable part is the pure dwell/cooldown/window governor in k1_mode_selection.

(4) Device evidence on K1 rules out beat-locked choreography today. On a 300 s music soak, tempo lock occupancy was 0.35–0.42 and the beat-quantised director failed. The anti-pin tempo change measured Δ −1.45 pp against a declared +5 pp target and failed. This independently supports the atlas choices R11 (groove flywheel with no tempo lock) and CANON:43.

(5) Per-band AGC is shipped and device-measured on K1. It fixes "louder gives dimmer" across bands (cross-band gain spread 0 → median 0.145 on Lateralus). It is still a 30 ms attack / 0.5 s release / about 0.2 s gain-settle leveller per band. It does not preserve build-to-drop contrast, so R09 must keep a separate long-window unnormalised level.

(6) EdgeMixer ships ON on K1 (split-complementary, strength 0.65, OKLab, centre mask, palette-honour). Its Captain-approved palette displacement is ±0.208 turns per strip, mixed at 65 % at the strip ends. That is a concrete anchor for R08's spread k (Titan path P uses a full turn per half today). The Titan EdgeColour port exists but only for donor modes, and it is disabled in v9.

(7) K1 DROP_CUT is the entry condition R03 needs: 120 ms of sustained quiet after recent loudness. Its instant relight is exactly the F-CAM1 defect (the riser relights the plate before the drop).

findings.what: K1 ONSET_V2 is a donor-shaped (Lightwave OnsetDetector) onset front-end over spectrogram[80]: log-spectral flux, a 14-frame median-adaptive threshold (×1.6 +0.05, floor 0.02), a causal 4-frame peak-pick with 30 ms refractory, and per-band kick [1,25) / snare [25,50) / hihat [70,80) triggers (EMA τ 525/792/1592 ms, K 0.8/1.0/1.2, refractory 45/37.5/22.5 ms). Its gate only permits or blocks output and never touches the detector statistics. It also drives a legacy IOI beat lock (300–1000 ms intervals, ±25 %). Status: implemented and compiled into the shipping k1_hardware build; host-measured; flashed to main K1 since June. I found no device-measured onset accuracy. The 2026-05-28 v1–v5 device evidence is for the earlier legacy dual-EMA Stage A detector, not V2. [FACT] v5 legacy: main 143 events/min, bench 92 events/min, no event storm, beat_confidence p50 0.0 / p95 0.5. [FACT] V2 host A/B on 12 tracks: onset proxy F1 0.031→0.098, recall 6×, survival on AGC-clamped input 115→923 onsets/min. K1 records 'DEVICE eyes-on is the one remaining gate'.

Its bass band is 62–250 Hz and its hi-hat band 6–12 kHz. K1 instead reused the post-AGC 80-bin Goertzel spectrogram.

The Titan removes the need. [INFERENCE] A Helium CMSIS-DSP rfft_fast_f32 of 1024 points is on the order of 10–20k cycles, about 1–2 % of a 7.5 ms hop at 1 GHz. At 24 kHz that gives 23.4 Hz bins, so a 47–250 Hz kick band is possible; this is the only K1-lineage route to onset timing below 110 Hz.

findings.what: Smart Director: implemented and compiled into K1 k1_hardware, but OFF at boot. Its config defaults to enabled=false; the boot scene is g_scene_smart='off'; scenes are runtime-only through scene.smart / :smart_scene. It classifies each tick into SILENCE/AMBIENT/STEADY/BUILD/DROP/BREAKDOWN/DENSE from post-AGC scalars, maps the state to a mode, palette and PHOTONS/CHROMA/MOOD/SATURATION scalars, and gates switches on onset or beat boundaries. Device evidence is status scalars only: the autonomy A/B 1101 vs 1401 is 'visual-judgement-pending', and no VPABB bytes were captured. [INFERENCE, arithmetic] energy_delta is the per-tick change of a 180 ms EMA. At about 8.3 ms ticks, α≈0.044, so the BUILD test (delta > 0.035) needs spectral_energy about 0.79 above its EMA, and BREAKDOWN (< −0.04) needs about −0.9. Both are practically unreachable and depend on frame rate. DROP is novelty > 0.45 AND peak_scaled > 0.55 on a single tick with no hysteresis, and it sets photons ×1.24. Frame-to-frame flips between DROP and STEADY would therefore modulate global brightness at frame rate.

summary:
Plain English first. The Lightwave library already contains working versions of the exact motion the Captain describes for "hits harder". Several of its effects draw rings that start at the edges and collapse into the centre. One effect records a wave and then plays it backwards so the light converges on the middle. On 17 May 2026 the Captain himself picked three of these effects as his approved "tension" and "impact" effects for the build and the drop. Nobody has carried any of it to the Titan: no Lightwave effect has been ported there, and the K1 ESP32 product does not ship the five Lightwave effects that were ported to it either. They exist only in bench/probe builds.

The library is also a warning list. Its beat effects invent a 128 BPM beat when the tempo tracker is unsure. Several effects flash near-white or keep a permanent brightness floor, which would break true black. Three of the eight DEC-009 presets (Aurora, Ember, Hush) do not react to audio at all. The show-level drop detector (SynqMatrix) waits at least 250 ms before it declares a drop. The useful part to take is the drawing ideas, used under labelled drop times first, not the triggers or the floors.

What I did: read-only. I read the canon, the Lightwave port assessment, the DEC-009 factory_presets.h, the effect ID table and the CoreEffects registrations. I mapped audio features for all 226 registration call sites with a script, read 20 effect bodies plus the SynqMatrix, TranslationEngine and NarrativeEngine code, checked git history including the Captain's Tier 1 commit 0e2e0778, ran claude-mem (DEGRADED mode, watchdog stale), and checked the K1 S3 platformio envs. No device, build, commit or write.

Inventory [FACT]:
- Lightwave-Ledstrip HEAD 4d71bc01 (dirty working tree, as the canon specifies).
- effect_ids.h:392 says "207 IDs assigned (206 active, 1 retired)". CoreEffects.cpp has 226 registerEffect sites; 20 of them (the 5-layer audio-reactive family, 0x1C) sit behind FEATURE_AR_1C_EXPERIMENTAL (CoreEffects.cpp:1386,1432,1446). That reconciles to 206 active.
- About 131 of the 226 registered effects are audio-driven: 101 read ctx.audio fields directly, 10 Beat Pulse effects go through BeatPulseCore and 20 SensoryBridge effects through SbK1Base. The other 95 or so are time-driven ambient effects.
- Feature usage: beatStrength 51 effects, chroma 55, rms 40, isSnareHit 35, isOnBeat 21, hihat 20, kick only 7, downbeat 4.
- Colour in the library comes almost entirely from palette index plus a global rotating hue plus a circular-chroma hue.

My 15 picks, ranked for "hits harder" and colour:
1. Beat Pulse Resonant: inward dual ring, edges to centre.
2. Time-Reversal Mirror Mod1: rewind the build so light converges on the centre.
3. Beat Pulse Void: true-black hit whose ring contracts as it fades.
4. Shocklines/Veil: power-four momentum charge that drives speed, never brightness.
5. Ripple ES tuned: sub-bass sets how fast the front travels.
6. Bass Quake: centre-compressed field plus a re-arm gate that waits on the front's position.
7. SynqMatrix: state machine and reason codes.
8. Transient Lattice and Saliency Bloom: a charge integrator plus a front sharpened by lateral inhibition.
9. Star Burst Narrative: key changes accepted only at phrase level, and a spatial triad (root, third, fifth).
10. EdgeMixer: per-state colour relationship between the two boards.
11. Progressive Ignition (0x1E04): fast-rise, slow-fall lit radius.
12. Shockwave Cascade: drop size shown as the number of echo fronts.
13. TranslationEngine: phrase change score plus a RECOIL gesture at phrase boundaries.
14. Kuramoto Transport: an invisible field that carries injected light.
15. Attack-Only Pitch Velocity (0x2101): colour updates only on attacks.

Each pick reimplements the behaviour in the v9 chain, in palette-position space, between depositV9/fadeV9 and outputV9 (inhouse_waveform.cpp:800-915 at 01ec2dc). The first trigger is the labelled drop times; R05 events come next, then R13. R00 bounds everything, and each falls back to host-006 when its own evidence is missing.

Ship path for any of this:
1. Today the behaviour exists only in Lightwave source, and in K1 S3 bench/probe builds for five effects.
2. Remaining steps: clean-room reimplementation with a provenance entry; a host bundle under the frozen EXT-v3 direction clause (atlas §9 Exp 1); R00 and the true-black gates; a device build, program and readback by the P6 lane owner under existing authority; a fixed-exposure camera strip.

findings.what: PICK 1 — Beat Pulse Resonant (0x1404; DEC-009 P5 'Pulse'; Captain Tier 1 TENSION). [FACT] Two rings contract INWARD, edge→centre. findings.what: PICK 2 — LGP Time-Reversal Mirror Mod1 (0x1B06; Captain Tier 1 IMPACT; SynqMatrix Transition default). [FACT] It integrates a 1D damped wave over centre distance 0..79 (cSq 0.14, damping 0.035, edge absorb 0.09). Impulses at the centre come from beats with a 16-frame cooldown, plus a timer every 96 frames. Every frame goes into history[1024][80], about 321 kB of PSRAM. After about 6 s forward it replays the history backwards for about 3.75 s with interpolation and a phase flip (u = 1 − v), so the waves converge back to the centre. Colour is the circular chroma hue (τ 0.20 s), plus gHue, plus spatial +0–36. Brightness uses a per-frame min/max normaliser (6 Hz follower, minimum range 0.05) and gamma 1.35.

findings.what: PICK 4 — Perlin Shocklines (0x0B01) and Perlin Veil (0x0B00): the footage-identified candidates (CANON §2; IMG_8285 shows Veil 77 → Shocklines 78 [R]). Shocklines also injects a ridge at the centre when 0.5·flux + 0.5·beat > 0.3; the ridge travels outward and decays ×0.90 per frame (τ ≈ 158 ms); treble sets ridge sharpness. Veil also shortens trails as music gets louder (fade 60 → 20) and maps RMS to contrast over 500 ms. The Captain capped Shocklines speed at 1 in the Tier 1 registry.

findings.what: PICK 9 — LGP Star Burst (Narrative) (0x0A06, most-touched effect file with 30 commits). [FACT] Two mechanisms. Phrase-gated harmonic commits: a candidate root/minor is adopted only after the phrase hold exceeds 1.5 s AND chord confidence ≥ 0.55 (or the effect is at REST). A circular EMA of the key root (τ 0.35 s) avoids an 11→0 'rainbow sweep'. Spatial triad colour: root weight is highest at the centre (1.15 − 1.65t), the fifth rises toward the edge (0.35 + 0.95t), and the third appears only in proportion to the narrative envelope 'env', peaking at t = 0.35. A burst adds the complementary root (+128) accent. The effect's own audio state machine runs REST→BUILD (non-quiet ≥ 0.65 s) →HOLD (bass > 0.14 after 0.9 s) →RELEASE (quiet or bass < 0.10 after 2.4 s). That is an energy envelope, not a drop detector.

A hard boundary forces a RECOIL motion primitive lasting lerp(150, 220 ms, beat strength) with brightness_scale 0.90–1.15. Tension is computed from rms, flux and rhythmic/harmonic saliency, clamped to 0.20 while in LOCK. Seven primitives: DRIFT, FLOW, BLOOM, RECOIL, LOCK, DECAY. NarrativeEngine (BUILD→HOLD→RELEASE→REST) is separate and purely clock-driven, with no audio reads.

new_levers_or_concepts: N-LW1 Rewind-the-build release (from TRM Mod1). Record the Titan's own post-deposit field during BUILD/ARMED and replay it reversed at 4–8× speed for about 150 ms at the drop, so the light converges edge→centre from the song's own build material, then release. About 128 kB per board for 2 s [INFERENCE]. Trigger only on an observed drop (CANON:43).

N-LW2 Power-four velocity charge (Shocklines/Veil momentum). Peak-held (level or onset)⁴ with τ_release ≈ 1.5 s drives scroll and advection VELOCITY, never brightness.
